name: Spatial Pattern Uniformity and Periodicity
definition: The degree to which structural elements are arranged in a consistent, predictable, and repeating spatial pattern with uniform spacing and alignment.
scale_0: Absent or not applicable: microstructure lacks spatial pattern uniformity and periodicity in the field of view.
scale_1: Minimal / sparse manifestation: features show some localized ordering or general consistency in spacing, but with noticeable irregularities or variations across the image, lacking long-range uniformity.
scale_3: Features show some localized ordering or general consistency in spacing, but with noticeable irregularities or variations across the image, lacking long-range uniformity.
scale_5: Features are arranged in a highly ordered, predictable, and repetitive pattern with exceptionally uniform spacing and alignment throughout the entire image.
scale_10: Features are arranged in a highly ordered, predictable, and repetitive pattern with exceptionally uniform spacing and alignment throughout the entire image.
description: The degree to which structural elements are arranged in a consistent, predictable, and repeating spatial pattern with uniform spacing and alignment.
scoring_guide: 0: Absent or not applicable: microstructure lacks spatial pattern uniformity and periodicity in the field of view.; 1: Minimal / sparse manifestation: features show some localized ordering or general consistency in spacing, but with noticeable irregularities or variations across the image, lacking long-range uniformity.; 3: Features show some localized ordering or general consistency in spacing, but with noticeable irregularities or variations across the image, lacking long-range uniformity.; 5: Features are arranged in a highly ordered, predictable, and repetitive pattern with exceptionally uniform spacing and alignment throughout the entire image.

name: Feature Elongation
definition: The degree to which individual structural elements or particles are stretched or extended in one primary dimension, appearing needle-like, rod-like, or fibrous.
scale_0: Absent or not applicable: microstructure lacks feature elongation in the field of view.
scale_1: Features are predominantly equiaxed or slightly elongated, with aspect ratios close to 1:1, or only a small fraction of features are elongated.
scale_3: Features exhibit moderate elongation, appearing as short rods or fibers, with aspect ratios noticeably greater than 1:1 but not extremely slender.
scale_5: Features are highly elongated, appearing as long, slender needles, rods, or fibers, with very high aspect ratios dominating the microstructure.
scale_10: Features are highly elongated, appearing as long, slender needles, rods, or fibers, with very high aspect ratios dominating the microstructure.
description: The degree to which individual structural elements or particles are stretched or extended in one primary dimension, appearing needle-like, rod-like, or fibrous.
scoring_guide: 0: Absent or not applicable: microstructure lacks feature elongation in the field of view.; 1: Features are predominantly equiaxed or slightly elongated, with aspect ratios close to 1:1, or only a small fraction of features are elongated.; 3: Features exhibit moderate elongation, appearing as short rods or fibers, with aspect ratios noticeably greater than 1:1 but not extremely slender.; 5: Features are highly elongated, appearing as long, slender needles, rods, or fibers, with very high aspect ratios dominating the microstructure.

name: Feature Occupancy Density
definition: The extent to which distinct structural elements or particles fill the available image area, reflecting both their concentration and the proportion of space they occupy.
scale_0: Absent or not applicable: microstructure lacks feature occupancy density in the field of view.
scale_1: Features are very sparsely distributed, occupying a minimal fraction of the image area with large, clear empty spaces between individual elements.
scale_3: Features are moderately distributed, occupying a substantial portion of the image area with some visible interstitial regions, but generally distinguishable.
scale_5: Features are extremely densely packed, nearly filling all available space with elements closely spaced, often touching or overlapping, leaving minimal to no empty space.
scale_10: Features are extremely densely packed, nearly filling all available space with elements closely spaced, often touching or overlapping, leaving minimal to no empty space.
description: The extent to which distinct structural elements or particles fill the available image area, reflecting both their concentration and the proportion of space they occupy.
scoring_guide: 0: Absent or not applicable: microstructure lacks feature occupancy density in the field of view.; 1: Features are very sparsely distributed, occupying a minimal fraction of the image area with large, clear empty spaces between individual elements.; 3: Features are moderately distributed, occupying a substantial portion of the image area with some visible interstitial regions, but generally distinguishable.; 5: Features are extremely densely packed, nearly filling all available space with elements closely spaced, often touching or overlapping, leaving minimal to no empty space.

name: Surface Irregularity and Texture
definition: The degree of texture, irregularity, and non-smoothness present on visible surfaces or along the boundaries of distinct features.
scale_0: Absent or not applicable: microstructure lacks surface irregularity and texture in the field of view.
scale_1: Surfaces and feature edges are predominantly smooth and uniform, with minimal visible texture or irregularities.
scale_3: Surfaces or feature edges exhibit moderate texture or minor irregularities, with some visible bumps, grooves, graininess, or wave-like patterns.
scale_5: Surfaces or feature edges are highly irregular and textured, characterized by prominent peaks, valleys, complex topography, or pronounced, dominant wave-like patterns.
scale_10: Surfaces or feature edges are highly irregular and textured, characterized by prominent peaks, valleys, complex topography, or pronounced, dominant wave-like patterns.
description: The degree of texture, irregularity, and non-smoothness present on visible surfaces or along the boundaries of distinct features.
scoring_guide: 0: Absent or not applicable: microstructure lacks surface irregularity and texture in the field of view.; 1: Surfaces and feature edges are predominantly smooth and uniform, with minimal visible texture or irregularities.; 3: Surfaces or feature edges exhibit moderate texture or minor irregularities, with some visible bumps, grooves, graininess, or wave-like patterns.; 5: Surfaces or feature edges are highly irregular and textured, characterized by prominent peaks, valleys, complex topography, or pronounced, dominant wave-like patterns.

scale_5: Interfaces between layers are extremely sharp and abrupt, showing a clear and distinct transition with no visible grading or blurring.
scale_10: Interfaces between layers are extremely sharp and abrupt, showing a clear and distinct transition with no visible grading or blurring.

name: Feature Dimensionality
definition: This concept quantifies the apparent dimensionality of the primary structural elements, ranging from point-like (0D) to linear (1D), planar (2D), or volumetric (3D) features.
scale_0: Absent or not applicable: microstructure lacks feature dimensionality in the field of view.
scale_1: Primary features appear as distinct, isolated points or very small, compact objects with minimal extent in any direction (e.g., individual nanoparticles).
scale_3: Primary features are predominantly linear (e.g., fibers, thin lines) or planar (e.g., thin films, flat plates) with significant extent in one or two dimensions, respectively.
scale_5: Primary features are clearly volumetric, exhibiting substantial extent in all three dimensions (e.g., large particles, bulk structures, or complex 3D architectures).
scale_10: Primary features are clearly volumetric, exhibiting substantial extent in all three dimensions (e.g., large particles, bulk structures, or complex 3D architectures).
